examples.ko: 전신주에 광고 쪽지가 잔뜩 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: Lots of ad flyers are stuck on the utility pole.
A typhoon hit and the utility pole fell over.

examples.ko: 차가 전신주를 들이받았지만 다친 사람은 없어요.
examples.en: A car hit a utility pole, but no one was hurt.

examples.ko: 전신주 위에서 작업자가 전깃줄을 고치고 있어요.
examples.en: A worker is fixing the wires on top of the utility pole.

examples.ko: 새들이 전신주 위에 나란히 앉아 있어요.
examples.en: Birds are sitting side by side on the utility pole.
Let's meet next to the pole at the end of the alley.

explain: 전깃줄을 걸어 놓은 기둥이에요. 말할 때는 '전봇대'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I'm waiting for my friend next to the utility pole.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 물건을 말하고 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the same thing and is more common in daily speech.

phrases.en: I put up a photo of my lost dog on the pole.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종이를 기둥에 붙일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when attaching paper to the pole.

phrases.en: The wind was strong, so the pole fell down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사고나 날씨 이야기를 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about accidents or weather.

explain_en: More formal or technical word; news and reports. It is the pole that holds up electric wires. In speech people also say '전봇대'.

t90.ax: A typhoon hit and the utility pole fell over.

examples.en: The plate fell on the floor and broke into pieces.
The window was hit by a ball and shattered.
Please be careful when throwing away the broken cup.
The plan I prepared for so long fell apart in an instant.

examples.ko: 얼음이 조각나서 호수 위를 건널 수 없었어요.
examples.en: The ice broke into pieces, so we couldn't cross the lake.

examples.ko: 휴대폰 화면이 조각날 정도로 세게 떨어졌어요.
examples.en: The phone fell so hard that the screen almost shattered.

explain: 접시나 유리 같은 물건이 여러 조각으로 깨질 때 쓰고, 계획이나 꿈이 무너질 때처럼 비유로도 써요. '산산조각 나다'라고 하면 훨씬 세게 부서진 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: The cup fell and shattered into pieces.
phrases.nuance_ko: '조각나다'보다 완전히 부서진 느낌이 훨씬 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It feels much stronger than 'jogak-nada', as if it broke completely.

phrases.en: I carefully cleaned up the broken glass.
phrases.nuance_ko: '조각난 + 명사' 모양으로 이미 깨진 물건을 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In the form 'jogak-nan + noun', it describes something already broken.

phrases.en: The window got hit by a ball and broke.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조각나지 않고 금이 가는 것까지 넓게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader word that also covers cracking, not only breaking into pieces.

explain_en: Intransitive: something breaks into pieces by itself. Use it when things like plates or glass break into several pieces, and also figuratively when plans or dreams collapse. '산산조각 나다' sounds like it broke much more violently.

t90.ax: The window was hit by a ball and shattered.

examples.en: I was angry and tore the paper to pieces.
I cut the cake into pieces and shared it with my friends.

examples.ko: 아이가 장난감을 조각내는 바람에 고칠 수 없어요.
examples.en: The child broke the toy to pieces, so it cannot be fixed.
After reading the letter, he tore it to pieces.
I took out a knife to cut the cookie into pieces.

examples.ko: 빵을 조각내지 말고 통째로 구워 주세요.
examples.en: Please bake the bread whole without cutting it into pieces.

explain: '조각나다'는 저절로 조각이 되는 것이고, '조각내다'는 누가 일부러 또는 실수로 조각을 만드는 것이에요. '깨다', '자르다'보다 결과가 여러 조각이라는 점을 강조해요. 목적어를 꼭 같이 써서 '무엇을 조각내다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: I cut the watermelon into small pieces.
phrases.nuance_ko: '잘게'를 붙여 작은 조각으로 만든다는 점을 더 분명히 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 잘게 makes clear the pieces are small.

phrases.en: The child broke the bread into little pieces.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조각이 많이 생긴 모습을 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It stresses that many pieces were made.

phrases.en: The cup fell and broke into pieces.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목적어 없이 저절로 조각이 될 때 써요. '조각내다'와 짝으로 알아 두세요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is used without an object when something breaks into pieces on its own, the pair of 조각내다.

explain_en: Transitive: someone deliberately breaks or cuts something into pieces. '조각나다' means something breaks into pieces by itself, while '조각내다' means someone makes pieces, on purpose or by accident. Compared with '깨다' or '자르다', it stresses that the result is several pieces. It takes an object: '무엇을 조각내다'.

examples.en: I set a mousetrap in the kitchen and caught a mouse.
I put cheese in the mousetrap.

examples.ko: 시골집 창고에는 쥐덫이 여러 개 있어요.
examples.en: There are several mousetraps in the country house's storeroom.
Where can I buy a mousetrap?
Grandmother caught the mouse with a mousetrap.
The cat is lingering near the mousetrap.

explain: '쥐덫을 놓다'라고 말해요. '덫에 걸리다'는 비유로 속임수에 빠졌다는 뜻으로도 써요.

phrases.en: I set a mousetrap in the storeroom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 덫을 설치하는 동작을 말하는 가장 흔한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for setting a trap.

phrases.en: A mouse got caught in the mousetrap.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쥐가 덫에 잡혔을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a mouse is caught in the trap.

phrases.en: There were no mice, so I put the mousetrap away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 덫이 더 필요 없을 때 치운다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the trap is no longer needed.

explain_en: You say '쥐덫을 놓다' (to set a mousetrap). The phrase '덫에 걸리다' is also used figuratively for falling into a trap or trick.

examples.ko: 공사장에서 크레인이 무거운 철근을 들어 올려요.
examples.en: At the construction site, a crane lifts heavy steel bars.
I can hear the sound of the crane moving since morning.

examples.ko: 저 높은 크레인을 운전하는 사람이 대단해요.
examples.en: The person who operates that tall crane is amazing.
There are many cranes at the port that move containers.

examples.ko: 고장 난 차를 크레인으로 끌고 갔어요.
examples.en: They towed the broken-down car away with a crane.

examples.ko: 아이는 크레인 장난감을 보고 눈이 반짝였어요.
examples.en: The child's eyes lit up when he saw the toy crane.

explain: 공사장이나 항구에서 무거운 것을 들어 올리는 기계예요. 같은 이름의 새(두루미)는 한국어로 '두루미' 또는 '학'이라고 해서 완전히 달라요. 인형 뽑기 기계를 '크레인 게임'이라고 부르기도 해요.

phrases.en: A tower crane stands tall at the construction site.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건물을 지을 때 쓰는 아주 높은 크레인이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A very tall crane used to build buildings.

phrases.en: The crane operator moved the load carefully.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크레인을 움직이는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the person who operates the crane.

phrases.en: My friend and I won a doll at the claw machine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인형 뽑기 기계를 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A name for the claw machine game.

explain_en: It is the machine that lifts heavy things at construction sites and ports. The bird called a crane is 두루미 or 학 in Korean, so don't mix them up. A claw machine is sometimes called a 크레인 게임.

t90.ax: They towed the broken-down car away with a crane.

examples.en: Books are piled up in a corner of the room.
A part of my heart kept feeling uneasy.
The child was crying quietly in a corner.
I tossed my bag into a corner.
I found a small doll in a corner of the shop.
If you leave a corner empty, it's convenient later.

explain: '구석'은 모서리 안쪽 장소이고, '한구석'은 '어느 한 구석'이라는 느낌이 강해서 '방 한구석', '마음 한구석'처럼 써요. 마음속에 작게 남은 감정을 말할 때 특히 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: somewhere in one's heart
phrases.nuance_ko: 크지는 않지만 마음속 어딘가에 남은 감정을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a feeling that is small but lingers somewhere inside.
phrases.en_equiv: in the back of one's mind

explain_en: Inner corner or quiet spot inside a space or heart. 구석 is the inner part of a corner, while 한구석 has the feel of 'one corner somewhere', as in '방 한구석' and '마음 한구석'. It is especially common for a small feeling lingering in the heart.

t90.ax: I tossed my bag into a corner.

examples.en: The teacher put the attendance book on the lectern.
Students who are presenting, please come to the front of the teacher's desk.
There isn't a single piece of chalk on the teacher's desk.

examples.ko: 교탁이 문 쪽에 있어서 들어오자마자 눈에 띄어요.
examples.en: The teacher's desk is by the door, so you notice it as soon as you walk in.
During cleaning time, I wiped the teacher's desk clean.
The blackboard eraser is next to the teacher's desk.

explain: 교실 앞에서 선생님이 쓰는 책상이에요. 교탁이 놓인 약간 높은 자리는 '교단'이라고 해요. 일반 책상은 '책상'이라고 하고, 교탁은 교실 앞 선생님 자리만 가리켜요.

phrases.en: The teacher is standing at the teacher's desk and explaining.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선생님이 수업하려고 교실 앞에 서 있는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a teacher standing at the front of the classroom to teach.

phrases.en: After class, I tidied up the teacher's desk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교탁 위의 물건을 치우거나 정돈할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for clearing or arranging things on the desk.

phrases.en: The teacher stepped onto the platform and greeted us.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교탁이 놓인 약간 높은 자리를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the slightly raised area where the desk sits.

explain_en: The desk or lectern a teacher stands behind in class. It is the desk at the front of the classroom used by the teacher. The slightly raised area where it stands is called '교단'. A regular desk is just '책상', and '교탁' refers only to the teacher's spot at the front.

en: to fail; to flunk; to fail a course

examples.ko: 다행히 낙제를 면해서 다음 학기에 올라갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: Luckily I avoided failing, so I can move up next semester.
If I fail this time, I have to repeat the first year.

examples.ko: 그 식당의 심사 결과는 맛은 합격이고 위생은 낙제였어요.
examples.en: In that restaurant's review, taste passed but hygiene failed.
To avoid failing, you need at least 60 points.
I'm worried I might fail math.
My friend is upset because he failed his English class.

explain: 시험에 '떨어지다'와 달리 과목이나 학년의 기준에 못 미쳐서 통과하지 못할 때 써요. 반대말은 '합격하다'나 '통과하다'이고, '낙제를 면하다'로 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: I failed the math course.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형 해요체로 이미 통과하지 못했다는 사실을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past polite form, used to state that you already failed.

phrases.example: 숙제를 안 해서 이번 학기에 낙제할 것 같아요.
phrases.en: I didn't do my homework, so I think I'll fail this semester.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 결과가 나오지 않았지만 걱정될 때 쓰는 추측 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A guessing form used when the result isn't out yet and you're worried.

phrases.en: I barely avoided failing.
phrases.nuance_ko: '낙제하다'의 반대 상황에서 아슬아슬하게 통과했을 때 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite situation: used when you just barely passed.

explain_en: Failing a class or grade in school (학기에 낙제하다) Unlike '떨어지다' for failing an exam, it is used when you miss the standard for a subject or school year. The opposites are '합격하다' or '통과하다', and '낙제를 면하다' is a common phrase.

t90.ax: I'm worried I might fail math.

examples.en: I argued with my friend over a small matter.
The couple often argue about money.

examples.ko: 말다툼하다가 서로 말을 안 하게 됐어요.
examples.en: We argued and ended up not speaking to each other.
I had a quarrel with my brother and went into my room.

examples.ko: 길에서 두 사람이 크게 말다툼하고 있어요.
examples.en: Two people are having a loud argument on the street.

examples.ko: 말다툼할 때는 목소리를 낮추는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's best to lower your voice when you argue.

explain: '싸우다'는 주먹이 오가는 싸움까지 넓게 쓰지만 '말다툼하다'는 말로만 다투는 거예요. 더 가볍게 티격태격하는 것은 '티격태격하다'라고 해요. '말다툼을 하다'로 풀어서 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: I had an argument with my younger sibling yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '말다툼하다'를 풀어 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A spelled-out form of 말다툼하다.

phrases.en: I argued with my friend over a small thing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로 이미 있었던 다툼을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form, for an argument that already happened.

phrases.en: After the argument, the two made up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다툼이 끝난 뒤의 결과를 이어 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to connect the argument to what happened afterward.

explain_en: Spoken — small everyday verbal quarrel, with family or friends. '싸우다' can include physical fights, but '말다툼하다' is a quarrel in words only. A lighter bickering is '티격태격하다'. You can also split it as '말다툼을 하다'.

t90.ax: The couple often argue about money.

examples.en: Meat grilled over a charcoal fire tastes different.
Sweet potatoes are cooking over the charcoal fire.
At the campsite, we started by lighting the charcoal.
Grill quickly before the charcoal goes out.
This restaurant is famous for its charcoal-grilled ribs.

examples.ko: 밀폐된 공간에서 숯불을 피우면 질식 위험이 있어요.
examples.en: Lighting charcoal in a closed space carries a risk of suffocation.

explain: '숯불에 굽다', '숯불을 피우다'처럼 짝지어 써요. 식당에서는 '숯불구이', '숯불 갈비'처럼 음식 이름 앞에 붙는 일이 많아요.

phrases.en: We went to eat charcoal-grilled food with my family on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숯불에 구운 음식을 말하고 식당 메뉴에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means food grilled over charcoal and is common on restaurant menus.

phrases.en: I grilled the fish over charcoal and it smells great.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숯불을 쓰는 요리 방법을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the cooking method with charcoal.

phrases.en: We lit a charcoal fire in the yard and grilled meat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불을 처음 붙일 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for starting the fire.

explain_en: It pairs naturally with verbs, as in '숯불에 굽다' (grill over charcoal) and '숯불을 피우다' (light charcoal). On menus it often comes before a dish name, like '숯불구이' or '숯불 갈비'.

examples.en: My friend got angry and snapped at me.
Don't snap like that. Talk calmly.
My younger sibling snapped at Mom and went into the room.
He always speaks in a snappy tone.
I'm really sorry for snapping at you for no reason earlier.
I saw a customer snapping at a staff member.

explain: 상대에게 날카롭고 퉁명스럽게 한마디 쏘듯이 말할 때 써요. '나무라다'보다 감정이 담긴 말투를 말해요. '쏘아붙이듯 말하다'처럼도 써요.

phrases.en: That person always speaks sharply.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말투가 날카롭고 퉁명스럽다고 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a sharp, curt way of speaking.
phrases.en_equiv: to speak in a snapping way

phrases.en: Don't snap at your younger sibling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날카롭게 말하지 말라고 부드럽게 말릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A gentle request not to speak sharply.

phrases.en: I held back, but finally snapped a remark.
phrases.nuance_ko: 참았던 감정을 짧고 날카로운 말로 드러낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when releasing held-in feelings in a short, sharp remark.

explain_en: It means to say something sharp and blunt to someone, as if shooting words. It focuses more on an emotional tone than '나무라다' (to scold). You can also say '쏘아붙이듯 말하다'.

examples.en: Please mix the rice evenly with the paddle.
A rice paddle is hanging next to the rice cooker.

examples.ko: 주걱에 붙은 밥알이 잘 안 떨어져요.
examples.en: The rice grains stuck to the paddle don't come off easily.
A wooden paddle feels better in the hand than a plastic one.

examples.ko: 밥을 푼 뒤에는 주걱을 물에 담가 두세요.
examples.en: After serving the rice, leave the paddle soaking in water.
We only need to buy one new rice paddle.

explain: 밥을 풀 때 쓰는 도구예요. 국을 뜨는 것은 '국자', 부침개 같은 것을 뒤집는 것은 '뒤집개'라고 해서 구별해요.

phrases.en: Please scoop the rice with the rice paddle.
phrases.nuance_ko: '주걱'과 같은 도구인데 '밥'을 붙여 밥 푸는 도구라는 것을 분명히 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same tool as 주걱, but adding 밥 (rice) makes it clear it is for serving rice.

phrases.en: I'll scoop the rice with the paddle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주걱을 쓰는 동작을 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for the action of using the paddle.

phrases.en: Please give me the rice paddle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당이나 집에서 주걱이 필요할 때 부드럽게 부탁하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to ask for the paddle at a restaurant or at home.

explain_en: It is the tool for scooping and serving rice. A soup ladle is a '국자' and a spatula for flipping pancakes is a '뒤집개', so they are kept separate.

t90.ax: We only need to buy one new rice paddle.

examples.ko: 그 학생은 큰 잘못으로 퇴학을 당했어요.
examples.en: That student was expelled for a serious offense.

examples.ko: 퇴학은 학교에서 주는 가장 무거운 벌이에요.
examples.en: Expulsion is the heaviest punishment a school gives.
A notice of expulsion came to the house.
He barely escaped the danger of being expelled.
My friend said he is worried about being expelled.
How are expulsion and suspension different?

explain: 스스로 그만두면 '자퇴', 학교가 학생을 내보내면 '퇴학'이에요. '퇴학을 당하다'처럼 말하고, 얼마 동안만 학교에 못 오게 하는 벌은 '정학'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: That student was expelled because of a fight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교가 내보내서 어쩔 수 없이 그만둘 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone is forced out of school by the school.

phrases.en: The school expelled that student.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교가 주체일 때 쓰는 능동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form, used when the school is the one acting.

phrases.en: He received an expulsion order.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공식적인 벌을 받았다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has a formal feel, as if an official punishment was given.

explain_en: Leaving or being expelled from school; formal, school records. Quitting by yourself is 자퇴, and being removed by the school is 퇴학. You say '퇴학을 당하다' (get expelled), and a temporary ban from school is 정학 (suspension).

t90.ax: A notice of expulsion came to the house.

examples.ko: 국수를 후루룩 먹었더니 금방 배가 불러요.
examples.en: I slurped down the noodles and felt full right away.

examples.ko: 뜨거운 국물을 후루룩 마시고 나니 속이 풀렸어요.
examples.en: After slurping the hot broth, my stomach felt settled.

examples.ko: 아이가 라면을 후루룩 소리 내며 먹어요.
examples.en: The child eats ramen with a slurping sound.
I slurped the seaweed soup and burned my mouth.

examples.ko: 바빠서 죽을 후루룩 먹고 바로 나갔어요.
examples.en: I was busy, so I slurped down the porridge and left right away.

examples.ko: 수프를 후루룩 마시지 말고 천천히 드세요.
examples.en: Don't slurp the soup; please eat it slowly.

explain: 국물이나 면을 빨아들이듯 빠르게 먹거나 마시는 소리와 모습이에요. 입을 벌리고 씹는 소리인 '쩝쩝'과는 달라요. 보통 '후루룩 마시다/먹다'로 써요.

phrases.en: I slurped down the juice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빠르게 빨아들여 마시는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes drinking something quickly by sucking it in.

phrases.example: 옆 사람의 후루룩 소리가 크게 들렸어요.
phrases.en: I could hear the person next to me slurping loudly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 면이나 국물을 먹을 때 나는 소리를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The sound made when eating noodles or soup.

phrases.en: The child slurps the noodles one after another.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계속 이어서 먹는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes eating continuously.

explain_en: It is the sound and manner of quickly sucking in broth or noodles. It differs from '쩝쩝', the sound of chewing with your mouth open. It is usually used as '후루룩 마시다/먹다'.
